nodes.title: develop is RED on the services/originate jest suite and NOTHING catches it — the suite is a blocking gate nowhere automated
nodes.description:
## BLUF

`develop` **is RED on the** `services/originate` **jest suite right now, and no instrument in this repository objects.** Measured tonight: 2 of 4 cells in `ks444-webhooks-create-description-guard.test.ts` fail on develop's own blob. **The suite is a blocking gate NOWHERE automated**, so the mainline can be red indefinitely and nothing says so.

Filed on Wednesday's ruling as a **new** ticket rather than folded into KS-961, because KS-961 is In Review and adding scope to an in-review ticket either reopens reviewed work or buries the new scope under a review that never covered it.

## The measurement

```
npx jest src/__tests__/ks444-webhooks-create-description-guard.test.ts   (in services/originate)
  2 passed   the two NEGATIVE cells (400s an object, 400s a null)
  2 FAILED   both POSITIVES - expected 201, received 500
  EXIT=1
```

Run on blobs verified byte-identical to develop: the test file is `229a3ccde` at both `origin/develop` and `b6884888d`; `routes/webhooks.ts` is `c88eb97db` at both. **PR #926 is the fix and it is open and unmerged**, blocked on an approval.

**Scope of the redness, which the QA gate did not measure:** the full service run is **48 suites / 509 tests, 1 suite / 2 tests failed** — the ks444 positives are the *only* failures in the whole service. ⚠ That run covers **48 of develop's 49** originate suites: it was executed on a tree missing `ks754-processed-by-widened.test.ts`, which is **unswept and named rather than rounded away**.

## Why nothing catches it — four instruments, each checked with a control

| instrument | originate/jest | control on the same file |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `scripts/preflight/preflight.sh` (13 legs, 428 lines) | **0 hits** | `step` -> 18 hits |
| `.githooks/pre-push` (244 lines) | **0 hits** | `preflight` -> 18 hits |
| 17 GitHub workflows | only `ci.yml` + `deploy-demo.yml` invoke workspace tests, **both** `workflow_dispatch`**-only** | 17 mention `test` |
| the 7 `pull_request`-triggered workflows | **none runs any service unit suite** | read their `run:` steps individually |

**This conclusion does not depend on the Actions billing state.** Even with Actions fully funded, no PR-triggered workflow invokes this suite. Actions being retired (Kam, 2026-08-27) is a second, independent reason.

## The actual gap

**The only instrument that would ever catch a red mainline is a human filling in a Test Evidence line — and it only fires if a PR happens to touch that service.** `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` requires `**Unit suites (touched services):** run/result | not run + why`. A suite that is red on develop and untouched by the current PR is invisible to that, by construction.

## The precedent that makes this concrete

`DEV-PROCESS.md` **has already made this exact argument once, for a different subject, and acted on it.** Cross-cutting guards get their own Test Evidence line specifically because, under "run `npm test` in the touched service", they *"execute only when someone touches* `shared`*, which is the change least likely to add a fifteenth service error handler"* — and it concludes **"A guard on no path that runs is not a guard."**

**The same argument applies to a red mainline suite, and nothing currently makes it.**

## Fix shapes (not a ruling - the cheapest is probably the third)

1. A preflight leg that runs the touched service's unit suite, so a red mainline blocks the next push that goes near it.
2. A periodic mainline run whose only job is to answer "is develop green" - no PR coupling.
3. A **baseline-diff** rule in the Test Evidence block: the author records develop's own result for the suites they ran, so "2 failed" is visibly pre-existing rather than silently attributed to the change. This is the same shape KS-660 already applies to Schemathesis ("the failing SET ... + its diff vs the develop baseline set, never a bare count").

## Related

* **KS-961** - the aggregate workspace suite never runs on a PR. Adjacent, In Review, deliberately not extended.
* **KS-1046** - `PREFLIGHT PASSED` printed identically whether 13 legs ran or 10. Same family: a claim whose check did not run.
* **KS-927 / PR #926** - the fix for the red itself.

## Ask

**Kam or Wednesday to pick a fix shape** (or rule that the red simply waits for #926 and no instrument changes). Nothing here is urgent in the sense of a live outage - it is urgent in the sense that the next person to read a green board about `originate` will be reading a false one.

*Filed by s162 (Platform K), 2026-09-09, on Wednesday's ruling. Measurement is mine and reproducible from the commands above.*
